text:
Sara: Heads up — dedicated-gpu-pool didn't scale earlier and 3 jobs in namespace tenant-alpha failed with Pending. CPU-only jobs were fine. Anyone seen CA/autoscaler logs?

Rik: Looking now. Saw something similar in eu-west yesterday. Do we have `nodeSelector`/taint issues or are pods just requesting GPUs that the pool can't provide? Any eviction events?

Maria: Pasting the pod describe snippet I pulled from one of the pending jobs:

```
Name:           render-job-42
Namespace:      tenant-alpha
Node-Selector:  pool=dedicated-1
Tolerations:    <none>
Events:
  Type    Reason            Age    From               Message
  ----    ------            ----   ----               -------
  Normal  Scheduled         2m     default-scheduler  0/10 nodes are available: 10 node(s) didn't match node selector.
```

Maria: Cluster Autoscaler doesn't seem to have emitted a scale-up request for this pod (checked CA logs for deds-1 group).

Jamal: Hmm — I remember we migrated resource quotas last week and the admission webhook added nodeSelector=pool=hosted-default for non-enterprise. If the webhook mutated some enterprise pods incorrectly they might lack tolerations for `dedicated=true:NoSchedule`. That would leave them unschedulable and possibly not trigger CA scale-up.

Sara: So tenants are using namespace-per-tenant model. We want enterprise tenants on dedicated pools, but CA isn't scaling. Do we rely on taints+tolerations or nodeAffinity? Which is the right policy for autoscaler compatibility?

Rik: Short answer: CA can only scale node groups if pending pods are considered scale-up candidates. Pods that have nodeSelector/affinity which doesn't match any existing node may not trigger scale-up unless CA can map them to a nodeGroup. Common pitfalls:
- nodeSelector pointing to a label no nodeGroup has (typo, wrong pool label)
- taints without tolerations (pods intentionally unschedulable)
- nodegroup minSize=0 + cloud provider constraints or CA scale-from-0 disabled

Rik: Check these quickly: the label on nodeGroup is `pool=dedicated-1`? Also CA config should include `scaleUpFromZero: true` for groups that start at 0.

Maria: Confirmed our webhook accidentally added `pool=hosted-default` to some enterprise jobs; that explains the "didn't match node selector" message. CA won't map that to the dedicated node group because the selector doesn't point to any dedicated nodes.

Jamal: Another angle — we set many dedicated nodeGroups minSize=0 to save cost. On GCP/AWS there are cases where scale-from-zero is blocked if instance templates require special disks or are zonal. Did we set `scaleFromZero` in the CA config? IIRC some groups had it off.

autoscaler-bot: autoscaler: scale up request for node-group deds-1 (+2 nodes, 2 GPUs) accepted — provisioning started.

Maria: Root cause: admission webhook mutated nodeSelector and didn't add the necessary toleration for `dedicated=true:NoSchedule`. So pods ended up targeting a label combination that doesn't exist on any group and lacked tolerations to be scheduled on dedicated nodes. I'll patch the webhook to add the toleration when it adds `pool=dedicated-*`.

Rik: Long-term recommendations:
- Use namespace annotation (e.g., `redwood/target-pool=dedicated-<id>`) rather than mutating every pod. The admission controller can translate namespace annotation to nodeSelector/toleration at pod creation in a single, auditable place.
- Ensure CA nodeGroup labels exactly match webhook output. Keep a single source-of-truth for pool labels.
- For cost: keep `minSize=0` for low-usage dedicated groups but enable `scaleUpFromZero`. Also set reasonable `maxSurge` and creation limits per region to avoid throttles.

Sara: Cost question — dedicated pools with min>0 are pricey. We want min=0 for most enterprise tenants, but then cold-starts hurt latency. Do we do scheduled warm pools for business hours?

Jamal: Scheduled warm-ups look good. Also consider fractional multiplexing on shared hosted pools for non-sensitive workloads to save cost. For strict isolation, keep dedicated pools but combine with network policies & KMS separation.

Maria: I'll push the webhook patch that: (1) when a namespace is marked `redwood/target-pool=dedicated-...` it adds `nodeSelector: pool=dedicated-*` and `tolerations: dedicated=true:NoSchedule` (2) leaves hosted default alone. Deploy to staging->canary. ETA ~2 hours.

Sara: Great. Please add a quick runbook entry: "If pods pending requesting GPUs and CA not scaling: check webhook mutations, nodeSelectors, minSize 0, CA scaleFromZero, and cloud quotas."

Maria: Patch applied to staging, canary passed. I rolled to prod canary group. Jobs resumed; last pending job transitioned to Running after autoscaler finished provisioning (scale-up ~3m). I'll open the PR for the runbook and the webhook fix.

Rik: Awesome. One more note: region GPU quotas vary (eu-west lower), so if a dedicated pool is constrained we should consider automated cross-region fallback for non-data-residency-critical tenants. cc @ops for cost implications.

Sara: Thanks everyone — great quick turnaround. I'll mark this as monitored and follow up on the runbook PR. :thumbsup:
